title: Oncogene-induced tumours can be prevented and normalized by managing bioelectric state

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Oncogene-induced tumours can be prevented and normalized by managing bioelectric state

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: Tumours induced by powerful human oncogenes can be prevented and normalized by managing their bioelectric state (e.g. forcing hyperpolarization), without correcting the oncogene.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2025, The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine › Cancer and the Scaling of the Self

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: (c) tumors induced by powerful human oncogenes can be prevented and normalized by managing their bioelectric state [175, 179, 180, 181]

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “The Multiscale Wisdom of the Body: Collective Intelligence as a Tractable Interface for Next-Generation Biomedicine”, BioEssays : news and reviews in molecular, cellular and developmental biology (2025), doi:10.1002/bies.202400196; section “Cancer and the Scaling of the Self”. Scope: Xenopus laevis embryos expressing human oncogenes such as KRAS (author's lab's prior work, refs [175, 179–181])

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2025-wisdom-17: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.72

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The causal contrast is strong and directly measurable. Existing experiments can test the Xenopus result, but uncertain raw data, durability and broad tumour generalization make the full claim only partially resolvable.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: In oncogene-positive embryos, compare tumour incidence and reversal after voltage-state manipulation with oncogene-only, channel-only and nonconducting-channel controls while verifying persistent oncogene expression. Prevention or normalization despite unchanged oncogene supports the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Developmental Xenopus tumours may not generalize to mammalian cancer.

Normalization needs histological and long-term endpoints.

Raw randomized animal-level results may not be open.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.9
data existence: 0.5
operationalizability: 0.95
analysis feasibility: 0.75
data adequacy: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Preventing or normalizing an oncogene-driven tumor by a voltage intervention, while leaving the oncogene in place, is a clean contrast. The published Xenopus experiments are not accompanied by a public animal-level dataset, and human cancer resources lack the bioelectric treatment arm. The result cannot be reanalyzed from open data.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Express a human oncogene such as KRAS in Xenopus and compare tumor incidence and normalization when membrane voltage is forced toward the normal hyperpolarized state, without altering the oncogene. Fewer or normalized tumors only in the voltage-rescued arm would support the claim; no effect of voltage, or rescue only when the oncogene is removed, would refute it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cancer genomic portals record mutations, not a bioelectric intervention with the mutation left in place.

Incidence tables for oncogene-only versus oncogene-plus-hyperpolarization arms are not deposited.

The rescue series has no public independent replicate.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:

data adequacy: 0.25
analysis feasibility: 0.25
operationalizability: 0.84
discriminating power: 0.55
